change.author: Joe Au-Yeung

findings.title: Salesforce connection setup calls prisma without importing it
findings.body: `getClient` now refreshes the Salesforce token on every construction (lines 75-84) and then calls `prisma.credential.update` at line 96. The import block (lines 1-20) has no `prisma` import, and nothing else in the file declares it. The call throws a ReferenceError (or fails type-check), so `getClient` rejects and `this.conn` rejects for every Salesforce user, whatever the sharing settings are. The refresh is not gated by any env flag, so every Salesforce calendar operation that awaits `this.conn` fails. `getAvailability` and `listCalendars` (lines 305-311) never await `this.conn`, so the rejection there is unhandled. Fix: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.
findings.originReason: The prisma.credential.update call was added by this diff and no import came with it.

verification.reason: The file has no prisma import. The bare `prisma` type-checks only because packages/prisma declares a global, and that global is assigned only when NODE_ENV !== "production". In production, line 96 throws a ReferenceError and getClient rejects for every Salesforce user.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sync asks for tokens by credential id, not user id
findings.body: `biginAuth` sets `credentialId = credential.id` (line 53), and `refreshAccessToken` takes it as `credentialId: number` (line 69). Line 93 passes that value as the third argument of `refreshOAuthTokens`, whose parameter is `userId: number | null` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3). When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, the endpoint receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>`. Whatever tokens come back are written into this credential at lines 102-109. That can attach another user's Zoho Bigin tokens to this user's credential. Fix: pass `credential.userId` (the user, null for team credentials) instead of the credential id, and thread the user id through `refreshAccessToken`.
findings.originReason: The refreshOAuthTokens call that passes credentialId was added by this diff.

verification.reason: credentialId is credential.id (line 53), and it is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, so the sync endpoint gets calcomUserId=<credential id>. In the current code the write is reached only if tokenInfo.data exists, and the sync Response has no `.data` (c5). Once that is fixed, the wrong-user tokens would be persisted.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh response may not contain `scope`, which the schema requires
findings.body: `salesforceTokenSchema` (lines 39-47) requires `scope: z.string()` and `token_type`. If Salesforce's refresh-token response omits `scope`, every refresh fails at line 90-94 with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Please confirm against a real refresh response for this flow. I could not check that from the repository.

verification.reason: The schema does require `scope` and `token_type`. Whether Salesforce's refresh response always includes them is a fact about the external API and cannot be checked from the repository.

findings.title: Google refresh reads `.data` from a raw Response when sync is enabled
findings.body: With the sync endpoint configured, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the fetch `Response` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15), not the `{res}` object from `refreshToken`. Line 94 `res?.data` is then undefined, and line 95 `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. The catch at lines 103-108 only rethrows for `invalid_grant`, so the error is swallowed and `myGoogleAuth` returns with the expired access token. The credential is not updated and the failure is not shown to the user. Fix: convert the sync response to the provider shape, or branch on the sync result before reading `.data`.
findings.originReason: Routing through refreshOAuthTokens is new, and it returns a raw fetch Response in the sync branch.

verification.reason: In the sync branch refreshOAuthTokens returns the fetch Response (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15). `res?.data` is then undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. The catch returns myGoogleAuth unchanged unless the message is "invalid_grant".

findings.title: Zoho Bigin reads `.data` from a raw Response when sync is enabled
findings.body: In the sync branch `tokenInfo` is a fetch `Response`, so `tokenInfo.data.error` at line 96 throws a TypeError. This method has no try/catch, so `getToken` rejects on every refresh. The same pattern is at zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:217. There it sits inside a try (lines 196-240) and the error is logged and dropped (lines 238-240), so the refresh fails silently and the stale access token is used. Fix both to parse the sync response into the provider shape before reading `.data`.
findings.originReason: The refreshOAuthTokens wrapping was added by this diff.

verification.reason: In the sync branch tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so `tokenInfo.data.error` throws, and refreshAccessToken has no try/catch. In zohocrm, line 217 has the same pattern inside a try whose catch only logs (lines 238-240).

findings.title: HubSpot refresh treats the sync Response as a HubspotToken
findings.body: In the sync branch `hubspotRefreshToken` is a fetch `Response` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15). `expiresIn` is undefined, so line 192 sets `expiryDate` to NaN. Line 198 then writes the Response object as the credential `key`. How Prisma serialises a Response is not verified here. Either the write throws and is logged only at line 204, or the stored key loses its token fields. Line 202 also passes an undefined access token to `setAccessToken`. Fix: map the sync response to `HubspotToken` before using it.
findings.originReason: The refreshOAuthTokens wrapping was added by this diff.

verification.reason: In the sync branch the Response has no `expiresIn` or `accessToken`. expiryDate becomes NaN, the Response object is written as the key (its token fields are lost), and setAccessToken receives undefined. Any error is only logged.

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced by the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted
findings.body: When the response has no `refresh_token`, lines 25-27 set it to the string `"refresh_token"`. Office365 then spreads this data over the stored credential (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264) and writes it at lines 265-272. A refresh response without `refresh_token` therefore replaces the real stored refresh token with a placeholder. Later refreshes send that placeholder and fail, and the user has to reconnect. The Zoom sync path has the same issue, because its minimum schema does not require `refresh_token`. Fix: keep the existing refresh token when the response omits it, and do not invent a value.
findings.originReason: The base spread only the parsed data, without a placeholder, so a missing refresh_token kept the stored one.

verification.reason: Office365's schema has `refresh_token` optional, so a response without it gets the literal "refresh_token". That value is spread over the stored credential at line 264 and persisted. Zoom's sync path writes `newTokens.refresh_token` into the key the same way.

findings.title: Zoom refresh sends appSlug "zoomvideo", but the app slug is "zoom"
findings.body: Line 92 passes `"zoomvideo"` as `appSlug` to `refreshOAuthTokens`. The app's slug is `"zoom"` (packages/app-store/zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16), and its keys are looked up by that slug (zoomvideo/lib/getZoomAppKeys.ts:11). A sync endpoint keyed on the Cal.com app slug will not find Zoom tokens. The other callers pass the real slug. Fix: pass `"zoom"`. Confidence is medium because the endpoint contract is not documented in the repo.
findings.originReason: The appSlug argument was added by this diff.

verification.reason: Zoom passes "zoomvideo", but its metadata slug is "zoom". The other callers pass their real slugs, for example "google-calendar".

findings.title: Credential update does not clear `invalid`, so synced credentials stay excluded
findings.body: The update at lines 73-80 writes only `key`. Credentials marked invalid stay invalid. Google sets `invalid: true` on `invalid_grant` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:112-117). `getCalendarsEvents` then drops them (packages/core/getCalendarsEvents.ts:17). A user whose credential was invalidated and then receives fresh keys from the sync stays out of calendar checks, with no error shown. Fix: set `invalid: false` in the update data.
findings.originReason: The webhook endpoint is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The update writes only `key`. The Credential model has `invalid` (schema.prisma:141), and getCalendarsEvents filters out invalid credentials, so a credential refreshed through the webhook stays excluded.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh runs on every construction and relies on statusText
findings.body: Every `SalesforceCalendarService` now makes a network refresh and a DB write before use (lines 75-99). Line 86 checks `response.statusText !== "OK"`. The reason phrase is not reliable across HTTP versions, and the error body is dropped. Checking `response.ok` and reading the error body would be more robust. Lines 92-94 are unreachable because the helper already throws.
findings.originReason: The refresh block in getClient was added by this diff.

verification.reason: getClient runs from the constructor and always fetches and writes. Line 86 checks the reason phrase instead of `response.ok`. parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, so lines 92-94 are unreachable.

findings.title: Schema computed keys look like they collapse, so the expiry-number rule is not enforced
findings.body: Lines 8 and 10 both use computed keys derived from `z.string()...toString()`. If zod's `toString` gives the same value for both, the second key replaces the first. The schema would then check only `access_token: string` and not the numeric expiry the comment at line 7 describes. zod's sources are not in this snapshot, so I could not confirm this. Please confirm the intended shape and replace the computed keys with explicit ones if needed.
findings.originReason: New file in this diff.

verification.reason: A computed key `[expr.toString()]` makes one property with one literal name, not a pattern over every numeric property. Whether the two keys collapse or not, "any number property is the expiry" is not enforced, and z.object strips the provider's other fields.

findings.title: Schema choice ignores whether the refresh went through the sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` routes through the sync endpoint only when `userId` is set (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5). This helper picks the minimal schema on the env flags alone (line 15). Team credentials, with a null userId, go to the provider and are validated only against the minimal schema when sync is enabled. Fields such as `expiry_date` are then not checked. Fix: pass the routing decision into the helper, or check `userId` here as well.
findings.originReason: Both helpers are new in this diff.

verification.reason: refreshOAuthTokens also requires a truthy userId before using the sync endpoint, but parseRefreshTokenResponse checks only the env flags. Team credentials (null userId) get a real provider response that is checked only against the minimal schema.

findings.title: Helper throws, so the callers' success checks are dead and Office365 lost its error log
findings.body: The helper throws at lines 21-23, so the `success` checks in zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:108-110, salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94 and office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 can never be false. The removed `console.error` in the Office365 refresh logged the Microsoft response body. That diagnostic is gone, and the error is now only the generic message. Fix: keep one contract, either return the result or throw, and restore the logging where it was useful.
findings.originReason: The base Office365 code logged the zod error and MS response, and this diff removed that.

verification.reason: The helper throws when `success` is false, so the callers' `!success` checks can never fire. The Office365 console.error with the Microsoft response body was removed.

findings.title: Webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time check
findings.body: Lines 24-27 compare the shared secret with `!==`. A constant-time comparison (for example `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers) is the usual choice for a bearer-style secret on a public endpoint. Exploitability over a network is low.
findings.originReason: New endpoint.

verification.reason: The secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time. Exploiting that over a network is unlikely, as the finding says.

findings.title: Malformed body and bad ciphertext surface as unhandled 500s
findings.body: `parse` at line 31 throws a ZodError on a bad body, and `JSON.parse` or `symmetricDecrypt` at lines 57-59 throw on bad ciphertext or JSON. None are caught, so the caller gets a generic 500 with no JSON body. Returning 400 for input errors would make the endpoint easier to operate.
findings.originReason: New endpoint.

verification.reason: `.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` all throw and none is wrapped in try/catch, so bad input surfaces as an unhandled 500.

findings.title: Concurrent webhook calls can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: The `findFirst` at lines 62-70 followed by `create` at lines 83-90 is not atomic. Two calls for the same user and app can both take the create branch. Whether a unique index on (userId, appId) exists was not checked. If none exists, duplicate rows result. Please confirm the schema, or wrap the check and write in a transaction.
findings.originReason: New endpoint.

verification.reason: The Credential model has only separate @@index on userId and appId and no unique constraint on the pair, so the non-atomic findFirst-then-create can insert duplicates.

findings.title: New webhook and refresh helpers have no tests
findings.body: The PR adds the webhook endpoint, the sync branch in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and the schema selection in `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, with no tests. The bugs above would be caught by tests on the sync path for at least Google, Zoho Bigin and Salesforce.
findings.originReason: The helpers and endpoint are new and come without tests.

verification.reason: No test or spec file references refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse or app-credential.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED holds the encryption key, not a boolean
findings.body: Lines 103-104 use `&&`, so the exported value is the encryption key string or undefined. Callers only use it in boolean contexts today, but any later log or serialisation of this constant would expose the key. Wrap it in `!!(...)` so the value is a boolean.
findings.originReason: Constant added in this diff.

verification.reason: With `a && b`, the exported value is the encryption key string (or a falsy value), not a boolean.

findings.title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is out of alphabetical order in globalEnv
findings.body: Line 207 sits after `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (line 206). The neighbouring entries are alphabetical, so move it next to `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`.
findings.originReason: Entry added by this diff.

verification.reason: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET sits after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY while the neighbouring entries are alphabetical.

findings.title: CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no documented contract
findings.body: Line 240 has no comment. A self-hoster needs to know the request (POST with `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` form fields, refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14, no auth header) and the expected response shape. Document both, and note that the endpoint must be keyed on the Cal.com app slug.
findings.originReason: Added by this diff.

verification.reason: CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no comment, and the request/response contract lives only in code comments in refreshOAuthTokens.ts.

findings.title: Redirect URI hardcodes the slug that appConfig already provides
findings.body: Line 17 uses the literal `zoho-bigin` where it used `appConfig.slug`. The value is the same (config.json:4), but config.json says the slug must not change, and the literal copies it. Restore `appConfig.slug`.
findings.originReason: The diff replaced `${appConfig.slug}` with the literal.

verification.reason: The literal "zoho-bigin" duplicates appConfig.slug, which config.json says must not be modified by hand. The value is the same today.

contracts.action: New POST /api/webhook/app-credential: creates or updates a user's Credential row from an encrypted payload
contracts.equivalent_path: none; no existing endpoint writes credentials from a server-to-server payload
contracts.before_after: New path. Gated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED (:19), a shared secret header (:24-29), then user and app lookup (:34-47). Writes key via update (:73-80) or create (:83-90).
contracts.visible_effect: The user gets the integration in their account without an OAuth flow. Calendar checks skip the credential if invalid was left true (see finding on :72).
contracts.failure_mode: Malformed body or bad ciphertext throws unhandled (:31, :57-59) and returns a generic 500. Concurrent calls can create duplicates (:62-90).

contracts.action: Salesforce connection setup now refreshes the token and persists it before building the jsforce connection
contracts.before_after: Before the change the connection used the stored access_token (the hunk removes no lines here; credentialKey is read at :73). After: fetch to login.salesforce.com (:75-84), statusText check (:86), parse (:90), then prisma.credential.update (:96), then the connection (:101-108) on every construction.
contracts.visible_effect: Every Salesforce calendar operation waits for a token refresh. The user sees a failure if the refresh path throws.
contracts.failure_mode: prisma is not imported, so line 96 throws ReferenceError and every Salesforce operation fails. Unhandled rejection of this.conn for getAvailability and listCalendars, which never await it (:305-311).

contracts.action: refreshOAuthTokens sync branch: POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT in place of the provider refresh
contracts.before_after: Before: each caller made its own provider call. After: when sync is configured and userId is set, the provider call is replaced by a fetch to the sync endpoint, which returns a raw Response. The else branch returns whatever refreshFunction returns, which is provider-shaped (Google returns fetchTokens.res, googlecalendar:88-89).
contracts.visible_effect: Credential keys come from the sync endpoint's response.
contracts.failure_mode: Callers that expect provider shape break: Google (:94), Zoho Bigin (:96), Zoho CRM (:217), HubSpot (:192). Callers that pass the Response straight to a handler (Lark, Webex, Zoom, Teams, Office365) are unaffected. The fetch has no timeout and no status check.

contracts.action: parseRefreshTokenResponse: validates refresh responses and throws on failure
contracts.equivalent_path: schema.safeParse on the provider schema (:18), the non-sync branch
contracts.before_after: Before (Office365, Zoom, Salesforce, Google): callers used safeParse and handled success (Office365 logged the error, Zoom and Salesforce rejected). After: the helper throws on failure, and the sync branch uses minimumTokenResponseSchema (:15-16). The success checks in callers are now dead.
contracts.visible_effect: A refresh that fails schema validation now throws instead of letting the caller decide.
contracts.failure_mode: Throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' (:22). The Office365 log of the Microsoft body is gone. Placeholder refresh_token is persisted (:25-27).
contracts.open_question: Does zod's toString on a schema return a unique key, so the duplicate computed keys at lines 8 and 10 do not collapse? zod is not in this snapshot (no node_modules).

contracts.action: Office365 calendar refresh now routes through the sync wrapper and the parse helper
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:262-264 before the change (refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse, console.error on failure)
contracts.before_after: Before: safeParse, log on failure, then spread tokenResponse.data when success. After: parse helper (throws on failure), then spread, then update. The spread at :264 now takes the placeholder refresh_token when the response omits one.
contracts.visible_effect: Refresh failures throw a generic error. A response without refresh_token replaces the stored token with the placeholder.
contracts.failure_mode: Stored refresh token replaced by the literal string 'refresh_token' (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27), causing a later reconnect.

contracts.action: Google refresh with sync enabled: response read as provider object
contracts.before_after: Before: direct refreshToken call, res.data read. After: refreshOAuthTokens wrapper; with sync, res is a Response, so res?.data is undefined at :94.
contracts.visible_effect: Token not refreshed; calendar calls use the expired token and fail later.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError at :95 is swallowed by the catch at :103-108 (only invalid_grant is handled). Stored credential not updated, and no error is shown.

contracts.action: Zoom refresh sends appSlug "zoomvideo" to the sync endpoint
contracts.before_after: Before: direct fetch to zoom.us/oauth/token. After: the sync endpoint receives appSlug "zoomvideo" (:92).
contracts.visible_effect: With sync enabled, the endpoint may not find Zoom tokens for this user, and the refresh fails.
contracts.failure_mode: Refresh failure surfaces through handleZoomResponse; the endpoint's response shape and key are not documented in the repo.
contracts.open_question: Does the sync endpoint key on the Cal.com app slug, as the webhook does (app-credential.ts:40-43)? If so, 'zoomvideo' does not match 'zoom'. The endpoint contract is not in the repo.

contracts.action: Webhook-created credential reaches the calendar list
contracts.before_after: Before: a credential marked invalid is excluded from calendar checks. After the webhook: only key is written (:78), so invalid stays true.
contracts.visible_effect: The synced integration stays excluded from calendar checks, with no error shown.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent exclusion until the user reconnects.

contracts.action: New module-level flag APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED read by the webhook and both helpers
contracts.equivalent_path: none; other flags in the same file, for example IS_STRIPE_ENABLED (:83-87), use !!(...)
contracts.before_after: New. Evaluated once at module load. The value is the encryption key string or undefined, not a boolean.
contracts.visible_effect: Credential sync is off unless both the webhook secret and the encryption key are set.
contracts.failure_mode: None directly. The constant holds the key value, so any later logging of it would leak the key.

contracts.action: Build the provider authorization URL with the state echoed from the add request (encodeOAuthState)
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-12 (moved from packages/app-store/_utils/encodeOAuthState.ts; the moved body is unchanged apart from the types import path)
contracts.before_after: Before the PR the same helper was imported from ../../_utils/encodeOAuthState; the helper is now at _utils/oauth/. No top-level _utils/encodeOAuthState.ts remains and no repo file imports the old path. The same call sites use the same helper, so nothing before or after the call changes.
contracts.visible_effect: The state is passed to Google as the OAuth state parameter and comes back on the callback redirect, where decodeOAuthState reads it.
contracts.failure_mode: encodeOAuthState calls JSON.parse on req.query.state with no try/catch. Malformed state throws out of the add handler, which returns a 500 with no catch in this file (googlecalendar/api/add.ts:17-41). This is pre-existing and not changed by the PR.

contracts.action: Decode the returned OAuth state in the callback (decodeOAuthState) to read returnTo and installGoogleVideo
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:5-12 (moved from packages/app-store/_utils/decodeOAuthState.ts; the body is unchanged apart from the import path)
contracts.before_after: Before the PR the same helper was imported from ../../_utils/decodeOAuthState. The helper moved into _utils/oauth/ and every caller in this part now uses the new path, so the value returned is the same.
contracts.visible_effect: state.installGoogleVideo decides whether the google_video credential is created and where the user is redirected (returnTo or the installed-app path).
contracts.failure_mode: decodeOAuthState calls JSON.parse with no try/catch, so a malformed state throws in the callback before the session check at callback.ts:23. This is pre-existing and not changed by the PR.

contracts.action: Persist the OAuth credential from the callback through createOAuthAppCredential (default export)
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:18-73 (moved from packages/app-store/_utils/createOAuthAppCredential.ts; the import path inside it now points at ../oauth/decodeOAuthState)
contracts.before_after: Before the PR the default import came from ../../_utils/createOAuthAppCredential. The helper moved and the callers changed to match. Export shape is unchanged: default export with (appData, key, req). The same signature is used in all 11 callers in this part.
contracts.visible_effect: On success a credential row is created for the user or team, and the callback redirects to the installed-app path or returnTo. The credential is what the app's calendar or video service reads later.
contracts.failure_mode: The helper throws HttpError 401 when there is no session user id, throws Error 'User does not belong to the team' for a bad teamId, and rethrows from throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam. None of the callers in this part wrap the call in try/catch (e.g. hubspot/api/callback.ts:50), so the request ends in a Next 500 with no redirect. No credential row is written on that path (the create happens after the throw). The error is visible to the user as a failed page load, not silent.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 1.** Part 1 of pr-11059 (credential sync and OAuth helper move). Four issues should block the merge: the Salesforce connection calls `prisma` without importing it, so every Salesforce calendar operation fails; the Zoho Bigin sync passes the credential id as the user id, which can attach another user's tokens; a Salesforce scope-field question that could also block; and the Google sync path reads `.data` from a raw Response and silently keeps an expired token. Other fixes: HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin sync paths also misread the Response; the parse helper writes the literal string "refresh_token" over a stored refresh token; the Zoom sync request sends the wrong app slug; and the webhook leaves `invalid` set. Consider-level items cover the webhook (constant-time compare, unhandled errors, race), the constant holding the key, an undocumented sync endpoint, and cleanups. Limits: `docs/adr/` does not exist in this snapshot, so there was no decision record to check against. The zod internals were not readable (no node_modules), so the schema-collapse point is a question. Import-only files were checked by a repo-wide grep for stale old paths (none found) and were not read in full. The adapter and calendar files were read in the regions the diff touches and their callers, not line by line.

**Batch 1 of 1, retry.** Reviewed all 20 files in this part. Every change is an import-path move: the helpers encodeOAuthState, decodeOAuthState and createOAuthAppCredential moved from packages/app-store/_utils/ into packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/. I checked that the new modules exist, that the export shapes match each import (named for encode/decode, default for createOAuthAppCredential), that their relative imports (../../types, ../throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam, ../oauth/decodeOAuthState) resolve, and that IntegrationOAuthCallbackState is exported from packages/app-store/types.d.ts. A repo-wide search finds no remaining reference to the old paths, quoted or unquoted, so no import or doc is left broken. I found no behavioural change in these files and no findings. Pre-existing issues in the moved helpers and handlers (unguarded JSON.parse on state, no try/catch around createOAuthAppCredential) are outside this PR's diff, so I recorded them only as failure modes in the contracts.

entries.title: Salesforce connection setup calls prisma without importing it
entries.originReason: The prisma.credential.update call was added by this diff and no import came with it.
entries.reason: The file has no prisma import. The bare `prisma` type-checks only because packages/prisma declares a global, and that global is assigned only when NODE_ENV !== "production". In production, line 96 throws a ReferenceError and getClient rejects for every Salesforce user.

entries.title: Zoho Bigin sync asks for tokens by credential id, not user id
entries.originReason: The refreshOAuthTokens call that passes credentialId was added by this diff.
entries.reason: credentialId is credential.id (line 53), and it is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, so the sync endpoint gets calcomUserId=<credential id>. In the current code the write is reached only if tokenInfo.data exists, and the sync Response has no `.data` (c5). Once that is fixed, the wrong-user tokens would be persisted.

entries.title: Salesforce refresh response may not contain `scope`, which the schema requires
entries.reason: The schema does require `scope` and `token_type`. Whether Salesforce's refresh response always includes them is a fact about the external API and cannot be checked from the repository.

entries.title: Google refresh reads `.data` from a raw Response when sync is enabled
entries.originReason: Routing through refreshOAuthTokens is new, and it returns a raw fetch Response in the sync branch.
entries.reason: In the sync branch refreshOAuthTokens returns the fetch Response (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15). `res?.data` is then undefined and `token.access_token` throws a TypeError. The catch returns myGoogleAuth unchanged unless the message is "invalid_grant".

entries.title: Zoho Bigin reads `.data` from a raw Response when sync is enabled
entries.originReason: The refreshOAuthTokens wrapping was added by this diff.
entries.reason: In the sync branch tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so `tokenInfo.data.error` throws, and refreshAccessToken has no try/catch. In zohocrm, line 217 has the same pattern inside a try whose catch only logs (lines 238-240).

entries.title: HubSpot refresh treats the sync Response as a HubspotToken
entries.originReason: The refreshOAuthTokens wrapping was added by this diff.
entries.reason: In the sync branch the Response has no `expiresIn` or `accessToken`. expiryDate becomes NaN, the Response object is written as the key (its token fields are lost), and setAccessToken receives undefined. Any error is only logged.

entries.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced by the literal string "refresh_token" and persisted
entries.originReason: The base spread only the parsed data, without a placeholder, so a missing refresh_token kept the stored one.
entries.reason: Office365's schema has `refresh_token` optional, so a response without it gets the literal "refresh_token". That value is spread over the stored credential at line 264 and persisted. Zoom's sync path writes `newTokens.refresh_token` into the key the same way.

entries.title: Zoom refresh sends appSlug "zoomvideo", but the app slug is "zoom"
entries.originReason: The appSlug argument was added by this diff.
entries.reason: Zoom passes "zoomvideo", but its metadata slug is "zoom". The other callers pass their real slugs, for example "google-calendar".

entries.title: Credential update does not clear `invalid`, so synced credentials stay excluded
entries.originReason: The webhook endpoint is new in this diff.
entries.reason: The update writes only `key`. The Credential model has `invalid` (schema.prisma:141), and getCalendarsEvents filters out invalid credentials, so a credential refreshed through the webhook stays excluded.

entries.title: Salesforce refresh runs on every construction and relies on statusText
entries.originReason: The refresh block in getClient was added by this diff.
entries.reason: getClient runs from the constructor and always fetches and writes. Line 86 checks the reason phrase instead of `response.ok`. parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, so lines 92-94 are unreachable.

entries.title: Schema computed keys look like they collapse, so the expiry-number rule is not enforced
entries.originReason: New file in this diff.
entries.reason: A computed key `[expr.toString()]` makes one property with one literal name, not a pattern over every numeric property. Whether the two keys collapse or not, "any number property is the expiry" is not enforced, and z.object strips the provider's other fields.

entries.title: Schema choice ignores whether the refresh went through the sync endpoint
entries.originReason: Both helpers are new in this diff.
entries.reason: refreshOAuthTokens also requires a truthy userId before using the sync endpoint, but parseRefreshTokenResponse checks only the env flags. Team credentials (null userId) get a real provider response that is checked only against the minimal schema.

entries.title: Helper throws, so the callers' success checks are dead and Office365 lost its error log
entries.originReason: The base Office365 code logged the zod error and MS response, and this diff removed that.
entries.reason: The helper throws when `success` is false, so the callers' `!success` checks can never fire. The Office365 console.error with the Microsoft response body was removed.

entries.title: Webhook secret is compared with !== instead of a constant-time check
entries.originReason: New endpoint.
entries.reason: The secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time. Exploiting that over a network is unlikely, as the finding says.

entries.title: Malformed body and bad ciphertext surface as unhandled 500s
entries.originReason: New endpoint.
entries.reason: `.parse`, `symmetricDecrypt` and `JSON.parse` all throw and none is wrapped in try/catch, so bad input surfaces as an unhandled 500.

entries.title: Concurrent webhook calls can create duplicate credentials
entries.originReason: New endpoint.
entries.reason: The Credential model has only separate @@index on userId and appId and no unique constraint on the pair, so the non-atomic findFirst-then-create can insert duplicates.

entries.title: New webhook and refresh helpers have no tests
entries.originReason: The helpers and endpoint are new and come without tests.
entries.reason: No test or spec file references refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse or app-credential.

entries.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED holds the encryption key, not a boolean
entries.originReason: Constant added in this diff.
entries.reason: With `a && b`, the exported value is the encryption key string (or a falsy value), not a boolean.

entries.title: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is out of alphabetical order in globalEnv
entries.originReason: Entry added by this diff.
entries.reason: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET sits after CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY while the neighbouring entries are alphabetical.

entries.title: CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no documented contract
entries.originReason: Added by this diff.
entries.reason: CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no comment, and the request/response contract lives only in code comments in refreshOAuthTokens.ts.

entries.title: Redirect URI hardcodes the slug that appConfig already provides
entries.originReason: The diff replaced `${appConfig.slug}` with the literal.
entries.reason: The literal "zoho-bigin" duplicates appConfig.slug, which config.json says must not be modified by hand. The value is the same today.
